summary: sitecard exposes installer workspace via public SSH gateway with default unauthenticated access
details: sitecard runs an AsyncSSH server (sitecard.gateway) that reads SSH channel input from a remote peer and writes it into a PTY/child process stdin, giving the connecting party an interactive shell inside the chosen workspace on the installer's host. The gateway is published to the public internet through srv.us (default), upterm, cloudflare, cloudflared, or devtunnel tunnels launched by sitecard.transports. The TokenSSHServer.begin_auth path returns False when config.accept is set, and `--public-access` is wired as the default mode, so a fresh session accepts any connecting party without an SSH credential check. The listener itself only comes up when the user runs the documented CLI, and the README advertises remote shell/terminal sharing as the product's purpose — so the capability is disclosed — but the public-by-default binding plus optional authentication means that merely running the tool exposes an unauthenticated interactive shell on the installer's workspace to anyone who learns or guesses the ephemeral tunnel URL. No credential harvesting, no auto-start persistence, no outbound exfiltration, and no hidden second channel are present; the control plane is the documented tunnel providers rather than an author-controlled host.
